Which of the following statements are true with respect to the function $y=f(x)$ whose graph is plotted above. 

- ${lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{-}}f(x)$ is finite
- ${lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{+}}f(x)$ is **not** finite
- $f(x)$  is  continuous at $x=-1$
feedback.worked_solution:
By inspecting the graph, we can conclude the following:

- Statement I is true. We get ${lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{-}}f(x)=1.$

- Statement II is false. We get ${lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{+}}f(x)=1.$

- Statement III is true. The graph of the function doesn't have a break at $x=-1$ and we can draw the graph of $f(x)$ around $x=-1$ without taking our pencil off of the paper.
